item.research_question: Can high entropy oxides (HEOs) be used as efficient catalysts for electrochemical water oxidation?
item.material_system: Hexanary high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with compositions such as [Al0.35(Mg, Fe, Cu, Ni, Co)0.65]3O4
item.processing_route: Sol-gel synthesis method using citric acid as the chelating agent and ammonia solution to maintain pH at 7
item.test_conditions: Cyclic voltammetry in 1M KOH with 1M methanol as the facilitator
key_findings: Non-equiatomic HEOs exhibited higher catalytic output current than equiatomic HEOs
Compositions with higher Cu and Al contents exhibited greater efficiencies toward catalysis
The maximum OER current density was 94.3 mA cm−2 using NEHEO with 2M methanol
HEOs can be used for further EC processes, including methanol oxidation
The catalytic platforms were stable over the experimental time scale
item.mechanism: The high entropy of mixing or stabilization, termed configurational entropy, is responsible for the formation of a single phase of as-synthesized hexanary HEOs
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of HEOs as catalysts for electrochemical water oxidation
quotes: High entropy oxides comprising six different elements were synthesized using conventional and facile sol-gel routes involving nitrates of all the elements
Non-equiatomic HEOs displayed higher catalytic output current than the equiatomic HEOs
Herein, [Al0.35(Mg, Fe, Cu, Ni, Co)0.65]3O4 is observed as the best performer NEHEO owing to higher peak current response, high diffusion coefficient, and rate constant values for WOR

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high entropy oxides (HEOs) be used as efficient catalysts for electrochemical water oxidation?. System: Hexanary high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with compositions such as [Al0.35(Mg, Fe, Cu, Ni, Co)0.65]3O4. Processing: Sol-gel synthesis method using citric acid as the chelating agent and ammonia solution to maintain pH at 7. Test conditions: Cyclic voltammetry in 1M KOH with 1M methanol as the facilitator. Findings: Non-equiatomic HEOs exhibited higher catalytic output current than equiatomic HEOs; Compositions with higher Cu and Al contents exhibited greater efficiencies toward catalysis; The maximum OER current density was 94.3 mA cm−2 using NEHEO with 2M methanol; HEOs can be used for further EC processes, including methanol oxidation; The catalytic platforms were stable over the experimental time scale. Mechanism: The high entropy of mixing or stabilization, termed configurational entropy, is responsible for the formation of a single phase of as-synthesized hexanary HEOs. Future work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of HEOs as catalysts for electrochemical water oxidation. Quote: "High entropy oxides comprising six different elements were synthesized using conventional and facile sol-gel routes involving nitrates of all the elements"
